messages:
emma: FYI escalation from Acme Analytics — customer on Dedicated (eu-west-1) using py-sdk 1.3.2. They report streaming chat sessions disconnecting mid-response; when the client reconnects it sometimes receives a duplicate partial final chunk and gets billed for the duplicated tokens. Pinging @eng-runtime @support. Repro snippet and logs below.

raj: Can you paste a minimal repro (client code) and raw SSE/HTTP logs? Also confirm whether they use short-lived tokens with rotation.

emma: Minimal repro (customer code simplified):
```py
# python async streaming pattern
async with RedwoodClient(token=ROTATING_TOKEN) as c:
    async for chunk in c.chat.stream(model='redwood-xl', input=prompt):
        if chunk:
            sys.stdout.write(chunk)
# background token refresher replaces token file every 30s
```
Raw-ish SSE fragment captured by customer (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
event: data
data: {"delta":"Hello"}

event: data
data: {"delta":" world"}

# next frame appears to be empty then connection closes
event: data
data:

# client sees EOF and reconnects, then gets repeated " world" chunk
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
They also attached SDK logs showing a reconnect at 2026-02-12T14:02:13Z and a second successful stream at 14:02:14Z with duplicate chunk.

kai: Reproduced locally with 1.3.2 using short-lived token rotation. Observed race: when token refresh triggers mid-stream we get a TLS reset from the edge as a side-effect of the auth proxy reconnect. Server sometimes sends an empty data frame just before EOF. The python async iterator currently treats that empty data frame as a legitimate chunk (yields empty string), then the reconnect logic replays last buffer pieces which causes duplicate tokens to be emitted to the app.

kai: Quick notes:
- Root cause likely in SDK iterator finalization + reconnect resume logic.
- Empty SSE "data:" lines are being interpreted incorrectly as final fragments rather than keepalive/empty.
- This interacts poorly with resume semantics that de-duplicate using a short rolling buffer.

chris: Eng-oncall here. I correlated the timestamps with autoscaler events — we had a pod preemption during that minute which returned 502 from the edge while backend was rebalancing. That explains the connection reset. Two immediate actions:
1) Short-term mitigation in SDK: ignore zero-length data frames when they appear immediately before a connection reset / EOF. Implemented as a filter in the iterator that drops chunk if chunk.strip()=='' and previous event was non-terminal.
2) Server-side: emit a deterministic final event when we intentionally terminate a stream (e.g., `event: done\ndata: {"reason":"preempted"}`) so clients don't treat empty data as meaningful.

support-bot: Ticket created: INC-6732 (https://redwood.internal/incidents/6732) — assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1 customer escalation.

emma: Customer asking whether the duplicated tokens will be refunded. They also sent request_id headers for the two streams: req_20260212_140213 and req_20260212_140214.

chris: Billing note: if we confirm the duplicate emission came from server-side reconnection (not intentional user retry), we can issue a manual credit for the duplicated tokens. Need to confirm by matching request_id and token counts (token delta around ~18 tokens duplicated). Please request the logs and we can process a one-time credit.

raj: Repro with curl (useful for infra folks):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/stream/chat?model=redwood-xl"
# watch for empty data: lines and connection resets
```
Example headers we saw that help correlate: X-Request-Id, X-Resume-Id, X-Edge-Instance. If customer can share those for both attempts we can correlate in logs.

chris: Proposed next steps/timeframes:
- Immediate: ask customer for request ids and attach to INC-6732 (Emma).
- Hotfix: patch py-sdk 1.3.3 (filter empty final frames + safe dedupe guard) — target EOD next day for a canary.
- Medium: server change to emit `event: done` on preempt and improve edge behavior on token rotation — rollout in 1 week.
- Billing: support to confirm and process credit once we validate duplicate emission.

emma: I'll collect the IDs and push the customer to install 1.3.3 canary once available. Thanks everyone, I'll update INC-6732 with customer logs.

chris: One more small workaround to give customer now (Python): wrap the stream iterator to ignore trailing empty frames and dedupe last N chars client-side until you see an explicit `event: done` or EOF for safe de-duplication:
```py
async def safe_stream(it):
    last_chunk = None
    async for chunk in it:
        if not chunk or (chunk.strip()=='' and last_chunk is not None):
            # drop likely-empty/frame-before-EOF
            continue
        yield chunk
        last_chunk = chunk
```
This is not perfect but reduces dup emissions while we roll the fix.

emma: Sending these notes to the customer now. Will follow up in the thread with request ids and sample logs.
